From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

I've reviewed the Seller's package against our playbook. Below are the material departures, my reasoning, and recommended pushback. Treating the Seller documents as the other side's draft, not instruction.

## Material Issues

### 1. General liability cap — Clause 12.1 (CRITICAL)
Seller proposes **20% / AUD 4,800,000**. Our baseline opening position is **25% / AUD 6,000,000**. The 20% figure is only a *conditional fallback* requiring prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft — **none has been given**. We cannot accept or even table 20% without that authority.
- **Push back:** restore 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not drift to the Seller's number by default.

### 2. Thresholds — Clause 12.2 (CRITICAL)
Seller proposes de minimis **AUD 25,000**, basket **AUD 250,000**, and **excess-only** recovery (only amounts above the basket).
- Our playbook: de minimis **AUD 5,000**, aggregate basket **AUD 50,000**, and **first-dollar** recovery once the basket is exceeded (tipping basket, not deductible/excess basket).
- Seller's numbers are 5x our de minimis and 5x our basket, *and* they've converted it to a deductible basket — a double give-away.
- **Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, first-dollar recovery.

### 3. Time limits — Clause 12.3/13 (CRITICAL)
Seller proposes **18 months** general claims period. Our baseline is **24 months**; 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval — **none given**.
- Separately, the catch-all "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" is a **hidden general-regime override** that would sweep Fundamental/Title/Tax/Fraud into the general limits. Reject.
- **Push back:** 24 months; strike the catch-all and carve out the separate regimes expressly.

### 4. Fundamental / Title regime (CRITICAL)
Seller wants capacity and title warranties under the **same caps and time limits as general warranties** "for administrative simplicity." This directly collapses the separate regime our playbook requires.
- Our position: separate regime, **100% cap, at least six years**, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- **Push back:** reject the merger outright. Separate schedule for Fundamental/Title.

### 5. Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance — Clause 9.3/12.8/20.5 (CRITICAL)
"Apply to all Claims of any nature" — there is **no fraud carve-out**. Our playbook requires fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct to be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and this is **non-waivable**.
- **Push back:** insert an express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out across all these provisions. This is a red line.

### 6. Disclosure — Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter ¶1.1–1.2 (CRITICAL)
Seller relies on **whole-data-room deemed disclosure** (everything in the data room as at 22 Sept) plus **public registers** and the statutory registers. Our playbook rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure in favour of **specific fair disclosure**.
- ¶1.4's blanket "nothing admits anything" reservation is standard but combined with blanket deemed disclosure it is very broad.
- **Push back:** require specifically-identified, fair disclosure against each warranty. Delete deemed/general disclosure of the whole data room and public records.

### 7. Buyer knowledge — Clause 8.3 (CRITICAL)
Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records." Our playbook: **delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions**; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- The "discoverable" language is a constructive-knowledge/prudent-search bar — doubly objectionable.
- **Push back:** delete. If any knowledge concept survives, limit to actual knowledge of named buyer individuals, and carve out title/capacity/fraud/indemnities.

### 8. Bluefen consent — Clause 3/6.3; Disclosure ¶2 (HIGH)
Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of revenue — clearly **material**. Seller offers only **"reasonable endeavours"** and treats consent as **satisfied on delivery** of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure ¶2 confirms **no final consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied** yet.
- Our playbook: require **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent; not consent-on-delivery.
- **Push back:** make effective Bluefen consent (with 11.3 conditions evidenced satisfied) a hard Condition Precedent to Completion.

### 9. Riverlark — Clause 2/7; Disclosure ¶3 (HIGH)
~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding, change-of-control at 8.1, discharge at 9.2. Seller proposes a **release following Completion** — and ¶3 confirms not repaid and no discharge yet.
- Our playbook: require **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases** at Completion. A post-completion release needs an **irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval** (not given).
- **Push back:** direct payoff from the funds flow at Completion with security discharge delivered at/before Completion. Reject bare post-completion release.

### 10. Employee bonuses — Funds flow; Disclosure ¶5 (HIGH)
DD-005 closing bonuses of **AUD 420,000** are deliberately **not itemised** in the funds flow ("a matter for the Seller"), and ¶5 notes **on-costs (payroll tax, super) are unaddressed**. These are Completion-triggered — economically a Seller liability crystallising at Completion.
- Our playbook: the AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Push back:** explicit funds-flow line item (or specific indemnity) covering AUD 420,000 **plus** payroll tax/super/on-costs, seller-funded. Confirm who bears on-costs.

### 11. Ironquay IP — Clause 11.1; Disclosure ¶4 (MEDIUM/HIGH)
Indemnity is narrowed to the specific SOW3 payment and called "adequate." ¶4 shows DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee, DD-010 shows **AUD 180,000 open**, and **no proof of payment or assignment** is in the data room — so IP title to deliverables may not have vested.
- Our playbook: **broaden** the narrow indemnity while **preserving the SOW3 cure**; the AUD 180,000 is **not independently verified either way** (don't concede it's owed, don't concede it's paid).
- **Push back:** broaden indemnity to cover failure of SOW3 Project Materials transfer/IP vesting and related loss, not just the fee; require evidence of payment and confirmatory assignment as a condition or indemnity backstop.

### 12. Export/privacy incident DD-006 — Clause 4.6/Schedule 6; Disclosure ¶6 (MEDIUM)
Seller downplays as "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material." Facts: download link to **unintended external address**, potentially **~1,240 records** (names, business emails, roles, timestamps). Disclosure correctly notes it's **not established** whether anyone accessed it, the scope, or whether notification is required.
- Our playbook: **assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction**; preserve logs, investigate, require updates.
- **Push back:** don't accept the "not material" characterisation as settled, but equally don't assert a breach. Require covenants to preserve logs, complete investigation, and provide updates; a specific indemnity for incident-related loss and any required notification/remediation. Keep it neutral on quantum.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals — Disclosure ¶8 (MEDIUM)
3 × AUD 110,000 = **AUD 330,000**. Seller calls them "ordinary-course operating costs." ¶8 admits it's **not stated** whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Our playbook: **assess**; **no automatic Debt classification or price deduction**.
- **Push back:** request the renewal terms to assess termination/accrual. Don't concede they are Debt, but reserve on price treatment pending the documents. Avoid Seller's unilateral "ordinary course" conclusion being baked in.

### 14. Title evidence — Disclosure ¶10 (HIGH)
Seller evidences title to 100% of shares solely by the **DD-012 share register** — a supplied internal source. ¶10 even notes the Buyer hasn't done its own verification.
- Our playbook: require **independent** title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; **DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof**.
- **Push back:** require independent verification — ASIC searches, share certificates, PPSR encumbrance search, board/shareholder authority, and a Fundamental title warranty under the separate regime.

### 15. Tax / IP "settled under the general regime" (HIGH)
Seller asserts tax and IP are **settled under the general regime**. This is a hidden attempt to drag Tax/IP under the weakened general cap/basket/time limits.
- Our playbook: keep **Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate**; no hidden general-regime override; Tax/IP terms remain **OPEN**; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Push back:** reject "settled." Keep Tax and IP as open, separately-negotiated categories with their own regime; do not accept them folded into the general cap/basket/limits.

### Minor / monitor
- **Office lease DD-007 (¶7)** and **Mossvale DD-009 (¶9):** Seller says notification/assignment restriction don't require consent for a *share* sale. Plausible on a share deal, but confirm by reading the actual clauses — don't take Seller's characterisation on trust. Low risk but verify change-of-control vs assignment wording.

---

## Summary of Recommendations

**Red lines / require principal authority — do not concede:**
1. Cap back to **25% / AUD 6,000,000** (20% needs Frost authority — not given).
2. De minimis **5,000**, basket **50,000**, **first-dollar** recovery.
3. General claims period **24 months** (18 needs Frost approval — not given).
4. **Separate** Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge.
5. **Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out** across all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance — non-negotiable, non-waivable.

**Strike the hidden overrides:**
6. Delete the "limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" catch-all.
7. Reject Tax/IP being "settled under the general regime" — keep separate and open.

**Disclosure & knowledge:**
8. Require specific, fair disclosure; delete whole-data-room, public-register and "discoverable" deemed disclosure.
9. Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion; any qualifier = named persons + actual knowledge, never touching title/capacity/fraud/indemnities.

**Deal mechanics / conditions:**
10. Bluefen effective consent **plus evidence of conditions satisfied** as a hard CP (not reasonable endeavours / consent-on-delivery).
11. Riverlark: direct payoff from Completion funds + security discharge at Completion (post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval).
12. Employee bonuses: explicit funds-flow line item / seller-funded **AUD 420,000 plus on-costs**.
13. Title: demand independent evidence (ASIC/PPSR/certificates/authority) — DD-012 register is not proof.

**Investigate / don't concede either way:**
14. Ironquay: broaden indemnity (preserve SOW3 cure); AUD 180,000 unverified — don't concede.
15. DD-006 incident: neutral stance — preserve logs, investigate, updates, specific indemnity; no admission, no quantum.
16. Sandbar renewals: obtain terms; no automatic Debt/price deduction.
17. Verify lease and Mossvale clause wording — don't rely on Seller's characterisation.

**One cross-cutting flag:** the Seller's package systematically tries to (a) adopt our *fallback* numbers as the baseline and (b) collapse every special regime into a weakened general regime via catch-all language. The theme of our mark-up should be re-separating the regimes and restoring our opening numbers — and I'd recommend confirming with Amelia Frost before any movement toward the 20% cap or 18-month period, since neither is currently authorised.

Want me to draft the mark-up clause language or an issues list for the Seller?
